rv.q: Ultimately, this is nothing less than an unpretentious art-history lesson, a great bittersweet love story and a close-to-the-bone consideration of art’s toll on the human psyche.
This is a spectacular revival and the principals are simply breathtakingly good.

Critical praise no doubt will help make the transfer a sellout, and the absence of their names at awards time will do nothing to remove Gyllenhaal, Ashford and the production itself from assessments of the season’s high points.

All the more extraordinary, then, that I felt unconstrained by the show’s built-in artifice and was swept up by the vitality and simplicity of this production adapted from the acclaimed concert performances of the work given to benefit City Center last fall.

This is a production for the ages, as good as it gets, a performance so exceptional, so overwhelming, you might be lucky enough to see something like it once, maybe twice in a lifetime.

cn.t: Critics praise this revelatory revival for Gyllenhaal's compelling debut and Ashford's warmth, with Sondheim's complex score beautifully served, though some find the show's cerebral nature and slow pace challenging.

sg.ra: SeatPlan, TickPick and Headout all converge: center rows D-K sit at a perfect distance to take in the whole stage without craning. Row A is called out as too close for comfortable viewing. Dress Circle overhangs at Orchestra row L and the Mezz overhang only becomes obvious at row R without significantly cutting the stage, so the middle band is protected. 2017 ATG restoration upgraded legroom throughout.

SeatPlan flags Dress Circle A-B center as offering unobstructed sightlines and the 'front few rows of the Center Dress Circle' as premium; rows D-F center are repeatedly called out as great-value seats with full sweep of the stage. The 258-seat section has a good rake and generous legroom. Balcony overhang only becomes obvious at row J and doesn't cut into the stage, so every row is usable.

SeatPlan describes Balcony rows A-B center as hanging close enough for detailed views and reports sightlines 'better than average' for a third level. Rear rows G-H are the cheapest in the house. Rake is very good, but legroom is tighter than the rest of the theater and the top of the stage may be cut by the balcony's angle. AVFMS user at G110 noted that some in-audience action isn't visible from rear balcony.
